name: TURKEY TAIL
blurb: THIN ZONED BRACKETS. BLOCKS SET HARD IF LEFT.

overview.v: One supplement company began with tinctures for its own health, moved on to foraged turkey tail and reishi, then partnered with farms for its raw material.
Cap n Stem keeps a turkey tail strain it knows well. Vials of it (Trametes versicolor #2, #3, #5) flew to the International Space Station in a school experiment.
Medicinal claims are unproven: the evidence is mostly from lab dishes or animals. When a customer asks on behalf of a sick relative, say so honestly and suggest a supplement at most.

cultivation.v: A matting species: the grain binds hard and breaks up far less easily than chestnut.
Blocks left too long become extremely hard and difficult to break up.

timeline.v: Usually 2-3 weeks before the plate goes in the fridge. A plate poured from colonized grain covered in about 5 days.
timeline.n: A remark in passing ("I think usually"), not a measured figure.

hazards.v: Treat every medicinal claim as unproven: the evidence is mostly in vitro or in animals.

notes.v: After the space flight its cultures recovered in about 5 days, while lion's mane was only just leaving the grain.

Tinctures: one extract maker uses about 1 part mushroom to 20 parts solvent for hard mushrooms such as reishi and turkey tail (1 to 10 for soft ones). They say beta-glucan lab tests show some ratios return more, and 1 to 1 extracts poorly.
Paper: one grower blends 100% turkey tail into water with a cellulose binder. The sheets are soft, almost like linen, and fold without cracking if dried slowly; dried fast they turn wavy and brittle.
